summary: Backend testing of new SuperAdmin analytics endpoint GET /api/plans/stats/summary. 13/13 tests passed (100%). Covered auth (401/403/200), response shape, MRR/ARR math correctness, per_plan ordering, total_companies consistency, cache-invalidation regression on PUT /plans/{id}, plan reassignment regression, and general regression (login, /plans, /support-tickets, /billing/checkout).

minor.issue: PlanUpdate Pydantic model does not expose price_monthly / price_yearly fields (only 'price'). The stats/summary endpoint reads price_monthly/price_yearly from the plan doc — with fallback to price and price*10 respectively. Consequence: superadmin cannot set differentiated monthly vs. yearly prices via API; yearly pricing is implicit (=price*10). If the product requires real yearly pricing (e.g. $6,990 vs $8,388), add price_monthly & price_yearly to PlanCreate/PlanUpdate + expose in the UI.

Companies do not currently have a 'billing_cycle' field populated; the aggregate defaults to 'monthly' via $ifNull. All 4 active companies are counted as monthly. If yearly billing is planned, the /billing/checkout flow needs to persist billing_cycle onto the company doc, otherwise companies_yearly will always be 0 and MRR from yearly subscriptions is undercounted (mrr = price_yearly/12 * 0).

Payments query filters by 'created_at' as ISO-string range. Works today because created_at is stored as ISO string, but if a future writer stores it as datetime, the $gte string comparison will silently miss rows. Consider standardizing on datetime objects.

action_items: Decide whether PlanCreate/PlanUpdate should expose price_monthly & price_yearly. If yes, add fields + update UI + backfill existing plans (currently only 'price' is stored). Otherwise, document that yearly = price*10 (default) and remove price_yearly branch from stats endpoint.

If billing yearly is offered via /billing/checkout, ensure the company document is updated with billing_cycle='yearly' when the yearly plan is purchased, so companies_yearly reflects correctly in /stats/summary.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routes/plans.py L205-206: uses `or` chain to compute price_monthly/price_yearly — this treats price_monthly=0 (Free plan) as falsy and falls back to `price`, which is fine for Free but hides the fact that price_monthly is not a first-class field. Recommend explicit None check.

backend/routes/plans.py L235: revenue query uses string comparison for `created_at >= since` (ISO string). Works only because writers use isoformat everywhere. Fragile — recommend using timezone-aware datetime objects consistently.
backend/routes/plans.py L250: sorted() sorts by -total_companies which puts Free (3 companies) before Enterprise (1). Product may prefer sorting paying customers first — verify with product.

PlanUpdate model (backend/models.py L373) does NOT include price_monthly/price_yearly — silently ignores extra fields from client. This can lead to confusing UX where UI seems to accept a value but backend drops it.
